mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous quarter - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages by more than 0.75 percentage points signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, resulting in neutral-to-negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 70% of quarters with GDPC1 < 1% for four consecutive quarters.
